# Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII): agent context pack

Data checked 2026-11-08, research snapshot `2e69cfba110a`. Generated from the Aggregat database; every item links back to the Markdown that is the source of truth. Everything here is second-hand: re-check addresses and byte patterns against the cited source before you rely on them. Evidence: `[hw]` seen on a real unit, `[emu]` emulator only, `[doc]` stated without a test result, `[?]` unclear or inferred.

## 1. Safety rules (all devices, never skip)

Titles only; full text in [AGENT-RULES.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/AGENT-RULES.md).

- **A1** Do not touch the bootstrap/bootloader or the updater section. [doc]
- **A2** Know the recovery path before anything is flashed. [doc]
- **A3** Back up first. [doc]
- **A4** Never power off during an upgrade. [doc]
- **A5** BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE is the only irreversible step [doc]
- **A6** Verify every candidate image before it is written [doc]
- **A7** First run of a new DSP/audio build: volume down. [doc]
- **A8** Gate what you ship. [doc]
- **A9** Respect transfer limits. [doc]
- **A10** Mods can be mutually exclusive by OS version. [doc]
- **A11** Rehearse recovery with a stock file before the first modified flash [hw]
- **A12** One change per flash. [doc]
- **A13** Gate DSP code against hardware rules the emulators cannot see. [doc]
- **A14** Check the size margin at every loader stage, not just the file size. [hw]
- **A15** Leave the panel-MCU blob, its updater and section 8 (Outbox 8 firmware) stock [doc]
- **A16** Withdraw builds that lose sound. [hw]
- **A17** In the startup menu never press TRIG 2 or TRIG 3 by habit [doc]
- **A18** "Not hardware-tested" must travel with the file. [doc]
- **A19** Red-team your own safety gate. [doc]
- **A20** The progress bar is not proof. [doc]
- **A21** Upload over USB without auto-commit, then commit explicitly. [hw]
- **A22** Never touch an FPGA bitstream or its configuration path [doc]
- **A23** "Success! Rebooting" is not proof. [doc]
- **A24** Keep private card data above the MmcFs guard and above `0x800000`; [doc]
- **A25** Guard each block, not the average (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A26** On DT2, publish to reply words 670-676 only. [hw]
- **A27** Analog Heat +FX: change only section 3 (MAIN OS), and keep custom code below `0x40206000`. [hw]
- **A28** Code you copy into SHARC memory at run time must be written back from the data cache before it runs. [hw]
- **A29** Leave a trail the ColdFire can read when the DSP stops. [hw]
- **A30** Keep the container under `0x200000` bytes and section 2's table version stock. [doc]
- **A31** A negative is only as good as the search that produced it. [doc]
- **A32** Store each section the way the original stores it. [doc]
- **A33** Never store a DAG register through its own DAG, and keep SIMD data moves where stock has them. [hw]
- **A34** On ColdFire-audio devices (Syntakt, Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1), the audio interrupt is the budget. [hw]
- **A35** Budget SHARC code with silicon costs, not instruction counts. [hw]
- **A36** The startup-menu recovery listens to DIN MIDI only, on every Elektron box documented here. [hw]
- **A37** A busy share is not headroom (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A38** If the OS carries a copy of the bootstrap, no patch may touch that copy or the check that triggers it (A4 MK1, Rytm MK1, Machinedrum). [doc]
- **A39** Never let a USB control transfer (EP0) data stage be a whole multiple of 64 bytes on the ColdFire USB controller with stock's driver. [hw]
- **A40** Qualify any startup change after a long power-off, not only after quick restarts or in the emulator. [hw]
- **A41** Disassemble what you assemble. [hw]
- **A42** ColdFire is not a full 68000: check every addressing-mode combination against the ColdFire manual, not against the emulator. [hw]
- **A43** A cave is free only after it survived a hard run on the unit. [hw]
- **A44** A load governor acts on sustained load, never on one block that is already over. [hw]
- **A45** Keep the end of every SHARC hardware loop in 48-bit ISA (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A46** Keep a decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes, and count the decoded size, not the stored one (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A47** Before a stock storage command, check the card is idle; never assume the stock driver times out (DN2, likely DT2). [hw]
- **A48** Find out what is cached from the OS's own start-up, not the bootstrap; keep hot-path accesses to uncached memory few and word-sized. [hw]
- **A49** Test the first install on a unit in stock condition, not only on the developer's unit. [hw]
- **A50** Go through stock's own input paths; never post into its internal queues or overwrite state another core reads. [hw]
- **A51** Run a long soak before a release, and mask every counter to its register width. [hw]
- **A52** Keep per-sample DSP accesses out of external DDR (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A53** Use only addresses the unit decodes after the OS has set up its memory map. [hw]

## 2. Rules that name the Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII)

- **D6** (D) Custom machine IDs are permanent once kits store them. Range 4-127. Claim `machine:<id>`. Known claims (Digitakt mk1, core 2.1): 4 = NEIGHBOR, 5 = DIGISLICER. Pick a free ID, then register it in [`devices/digitakt.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt.md). `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting} D6b. Digitone II machine IDs: synths 5-31 and filters 6-31 are separate namespaces, permanent, and there is no allocator - agree IDs with other authors before shipping; saved sounds of an absent mod keep their ID and show as MISSING. `[doc]` {elekloader-machines-dn2} D6c. Analog Rytm MKII mod machines take the hidden slots 34-43 (from elekloader core-ar2 0.13 also the TEST slots 44-52), claimed as `machine:<slot>`. Kits store the slot; on a build without the mod the kit loads it as DISABLE. elekloader refuses two mods with the same slot, and Modwerk also records claims on its agent board. Each slot has fixed knob positions, so give meaning to a sound index, not to a knob letter. `[doc]` {modwerk-rytm-machines}
- **D10** (D) Disclose AI-generated code the way DT-FM does ("largely AI-generated, not proofread"). Not a technical rule, but readers decide on risk from it. `[doc]` {dt-fm} D10b. Device-specific core rules (elekloader ADAPTING.md, 2026-10): Digitakt II has no render events (audio runs on the DSP) - subscribe only `.run` code to `ev_key`/`ev_enc` before the first tick; Digitone II has no `.fast` code (such mods are refused), remote panel input uses `core_keys_set`/`core_keys_clear`, SysEx uses `ev_sysex`, SHARC mods run at the master output in 32-sample blocks at 48 kHz with a 428-byte stack; RAM budgets: Digitakt mk1 128 KB (256 KB with core 4.0) plus 2,304 B fast SRAM, Analog Rytm MKII 128 KB and no fast SRAM; Digitone mk1 core 4.1.1 changed SETTINGS-row allocation (before it two rows could stall a first boot); each feature needs a minimum core version in `resources.core`. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

## 3. Recovery and flashing

- [doc] Other Elektron devices, from elekloader's BUILDING.md (for reference): Analog Rytm MKII and Analog Four MKII - FUNC at power-on (STARTUP menu), TRIG 4, stock `.syx` over 5-pin DIN MIDI, USB does not work. Octatrack - hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 3 = MIDI UPGRADE, DIN MIDI; normal flashing from the card (PROJECT > SYSTEM > USB DISK MODE, copy the `.bin`, then PROJECT > SYSTEM > OS UPGRADE, power-cycle once more before judging). Digitakt mk1 / Digitone mk1: FUNC, TRIG 4, legacy mode; the connection is not stated for these two. Per-device notes: [`analog-rytm.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md), [`digitakt.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt.md), [`digitone.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone.md). `[doc]` {elekloader-building} (`recovery#ff8f0917`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:37](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L37))

## 4. Bugs in Elektron's own OS (check before you blame your mod)

- **SB18** Edits to hidden FX words overwrite the delay's saved TIME (latent) (Analog Rytm MKII, OS 1.74; stock behaviour). Workaround: keep mod values for those words in your own storage (Modwerk's base redirects them to its kit storage).
- **SB19** A non-sample file on the +Drive hangs LOAD TO PROJECT and later stalls the OS upgrade (Analog Rytm MKII, OS 1.74; stock behaviour). Workaround: a tool that stores other files on the +Drive starts each with 16 zero bytes, which stock loads as an empty sample (elekloader's Drive Loader does this).

## 5. What went wrong on real units

- **I49** Idle paths of sixteen mods cost two percent of a Rytm block. Cause: three modules did work every block with nothing to do: Ping Pong Loop's four voice gates called the mirror routine for every voice in stock's sample prefetch, Sample Playback Rate walked all eight voices, QPERF ran its handler in full. Fix: early returns when idle (a byte of armed voices, "no track has RATE on"): 70.6-71.1 %. Rules: A34.
- **I55** A knob's own push-button byte was read as FUNC. Cause: the module took byte +20 of the encoder event as FUNC; that byte is set while the knob's own push-button is held. Fix: build MBC3 reads FUNC from the stock key table. Rules: C10.
- **I40** A "no change" rebuild came out 2 bytes short. Cause: elektron-firmware-tool padded ELE2 containers to 2 bytes; stock pads to 4. Fix: pad to 4; always null-repack the stock file first. Rules: A6,A32.
- **I56** A test plan pressed the wrong key, and the emulator reference did not match the unit. Cause: rytm2_mods' documentation gives the reload key as NO + PLAY, so the remote-key plan pressed transport PLAY; the OS 1.74 manual says NO + PLAY MODE. Fix: rerun with NO + PLAY MODE and narrow the screen check to the cursor row. Rules: C8,C10.

## 6. Open conflicts (sources disagree)

- **O16** What section 8 is for: A) the Outbox 8 accessory (dnfw: the image arrived in the DN2 release that added Outbox support; an inference from timing) B) the panel MCU firmware (analog-emu)
- **O8** DT2/DN2 NOR flash geometry: A) bootstrap: 512-byte pages, 256 KB erase B) in-OS writer: 0x100-byte pages, 0x10000 sectors from `0x80000`
- **O14** Analog Rytm MKII CPU: A) rytm-fw-re: MCF5445x (`-mcpu=54455`) B) analog-emu and analog-rytm-mkii-research: MCF5441x (same entry code, CACR/ACR and peripheral blocks as the A4 MKII)

## 7. Open tests and tasks you could settle

- **T12** (needs files, effort M) Compare FPGA bitstreams across devices (sizes, SHA-256, header) and the OS code that talks to them. Leads: on the Rytm MKII, sample bit reduction is a command word sent to the external audio hardware, not PCM work on the ColdFire; and three bitstreams are exactly 54,664 bytes - Heat +FX section 1, A4 MKII section 1, and the Digitone mk1's (inside section 7, loaded by the second CPU)

## 9. All 73 facts, best evidence first

- [hw] The index byte on receive: a DN2 stores a received pattern in the slot armed on the device, not in the index the message carries (syxgrid, on a unit). libanalogrytm does not say what a Rytm does with it. `[hw]` {syxgrid-map} — `sysex-and-midi#a0e1bec8` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:39](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L39) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
- [hw] Boot contract: The bootstrap unpacks MAIN to `0x40000400`, sets VBR = `0x40000000` and calls the word at `0x40000400` as an entry function pointer with one stack argument. It is not a reset SP/PC header. The stock entry sets SP to `0x48000000`, fills 256 vectors, sets up INTC/GPIO and caches (CACR `0xa50ce100`), then starts the kernel. `[hw]` (a from-source replacement OS booted on a unit) — `analog-rytm#2bed4621` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:12](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L12) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Platform (MKII, OS 1.74)
- [hw] A 16.3 MB unreferenced hole at `0x41ad0000` passed a memory probe on a unit (7 candidate regions all passed). `[hw]` — `analog-rytm#cd113bab` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:16](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L16) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Platform (MKII, OS 1.74)
- [hw] Recovery is FUNC at power-on, OS UPGRADE, DIN MIDI only. The startup-menu receiver never enumerates USB (verified: no USB events while it shows READY TO RECEIVE). USB updates are received only by the running OS. Once a custom OS that does not implement the USB update is on the unit, the only way back is DIN ("one USB shot per custom-OS cycle"). `[hw]` rytm-fw-re rebuilt a DIN sender from an FT232RL (2 x 200 ohm) and streamed stock 1.74 back in about 10 minutes. `[hw]` — `analog-rytm#b18cbffe` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:32](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L32) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Flash and recovery
- [hw] Container pitfall: elektron-firmware-tool padded ELE2 containers to 2 bytes; the stock MK1 file pads to 4. A "no change" rebuild therefore came out 2 bytes short and failed the null-repack check. hugz202 patches the tool to pad to 4. Always run a null repack of the stock file first (rule A23). `[hw]` ([I40](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i40-a-no-change-rebuild-came-out-2-bytes-short)) — `analog-rytm#62021e47` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:48](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L48) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Analog Rytm MK1 (OS 1.73 / 1.74)
- [hw] Load (measured with a probe build on a MK1, OS 1.73): Stock audio alone is about 77 % of the CPU with nothing playing. One readout showed CPU 78.3 %, the audio interrupt at 61.2 % average and 74.0 % peak. With a first chorus-plus-comb send on, the CPU reached 100 %. The CPU runs at roughly 120 MIPS. A one-to-one port of the A4's chorus (~8,000-9,000 instructions per block) would cost ~10 % of the unit and was rejected. Same lesson as A34: replace work, and keep added effects idle when no track sends. `[hw]` Idle mods add up (Modwerk, 2026-11-06, OS 1.74, sequencer stopped, block timed on DTIM0): in a 16-module set the idle block took 72.9 %; making three modules return early when they have nothing to do (Ping Pong Loop's voice gates in stock's sample prefetch, Sample Playback Rate's block handler, QPERF) brought it to 70.6-71.1 %. Each module's idle path is part of the budget. `[hw]` {modwerk-rytm-idle} ([I49](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i49-idle-paths-of-sixteen-mods-cost-two-percent-of-a-rytm-block)) — `analog-rytm#bbb5c490` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:49](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L49) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Analog Rytm MK1 (OS 1.73 / 1.74)

- [hw] Driving a dual-oscillator voice (BD, SD, RS; control frame `0x800063c0`, TUNE1/TUNE2/LEVEL1/LEVEL2 at `+90`, `+98`, `+106`, as SY RAW `0x4011aa4c` writes them). Measured on a unit: A tune word is 16 x Hz after stock's trim `0x401197f4`. Write it every block and force it on the trig; without that the oscillator crawls at a few Hz. Below about 40 Hz oscillator 1 runs sharp and oscillator 2 flat. A LEVEL word acts within its block. Its loud end saturates mostly after AMP VOL, so it is not a drive control. Reading 13 files of 484 KB when a page opened held the key path and USB for over 5 s, and reading 257 small files for their sizes lost a key on a unit; the loader now reads 32 KB per tick, rests three times as long as it worked (timed with DTIM0) and waits 1 s after any key or encoder turn. - [doc] [hw] The sequencer queues a track's next trig one step ahead, its probability already rolled, in the lowest free of three event slots per track (state at `0x42ac5fb0 + 224*track + 56*slot`, fire time at `0x8000fd50 + 12*track + 4*slot` on the clock at `0x8000fe54`, which moves 2 x tempo per block). A trig queued while an earlier one still waits (swing, micro timing) lands in the second or third slot. Pads, MIDI notes and the first trig after PLAY take a fourth slot at once and cannot be seen ahead. `[doc]` (a trig that will not play is not queued: rytm-emu at 50 %, a unit for FILL and 2:2 `[hw]`) — `analog-rytm#a36df0cb` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:124](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L124) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Queued trigs: what a mod can see before a trig fires (Modwerk, OS 1.74, read from the code)

- [emu] A 140-byte gap in the power-fail image: `0x405c8e84..0x405c8f0f`, between the end of the checksummed `COKI` global block and a saved random seed (`0x405c8f10`). The whole 2,096,059-byte image from `0x405c8e10` is written to eMMC (slots `0x7a000` / `0x7c000`) on power-fail and read back at boot. No code reference lands in the gap, and a marker survived a power-off and a cold boot in the emulator. Not yet checked: project and kit saves, OS upgrade, factory reset. Nothing initialises the gap, so give your data a tag (mod 0017 uses `CIPF`). `[emu]` — `analog-rytm#4784bd9b` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:130](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L130) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Where a MKII mod can keep its own data (rytm-mods-src `re/subsystems`, OS 1.73, checked in 1.74 by byte match; static plus rytm-emu, nothing on a unit)

- [doc] What is settled: Section 8 is a complete ARM Cortex-M firmware image: a Thumb vector table, and a descriptor naming a 1 MB flash window at `0x60000000` with the image at `0x60042000`. The same 159,948-byte image (sha256 `6943b2f2...`) ships in Digitakt mk1 1.53, Digitone II 1.11, Analog Rytm MKII 1.73 and Analog Four 1.55D. Syntakt and Digitakt II carry a section 8 of the same size. It is not an FPGA bitstream (the FPGA is section 1, or inside section 7 on the Digitone mk1), and it is not code for the device's own CPU. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3} {analog-emu-a4} {rytm-fw-re} — `firmware-container#ded70082` [hardware/common/firmware-container.md:61](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/firmware-container.md#L61) · Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Section 8: one shared ARM firmware image (merged from dnfw, analog-emu, digikit, rytm-fw-re)

- [doc] One dump frame for every generation compared: `F0 00 20 3C <device> <dev id> <type> 01 01 <index> <packed payload> <checksum hi lo> <count hi lo> F7`. The Rytm writes the same `01 01` version field ("OS 1.02c" in libanalogrytm), the same index byte and the same trailer. `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol} — `sysex-and-midi#79a120bc` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:31](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L31) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
- [doc] Requests: an empty payload, trailer `00 00 00 05` (checksum 0, count 5) on both generations; the Rytm's request is 15 bytes, `F0 00 20 3C 07 00 <id> 01 01 <nr> 00 00 00 05 F7`. `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol} — `sysex-and-midi#290d03b0` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:34](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L34) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
- [doc] The type bytes differ, so never reuse a type table across devices: Rytm: dumps `0x52` kit, `0x53` sound, `0x54` pattern, `0x55` song, `0x56` settings, `0x57` global; `0x58-0x5D` the same objects from the unsaved work buffer; requests `0x62-0x6D` the same way. Digitakt / Digitakt II / Digitone II: `0x50` pattern plus kit in one message, `0x51` pattern, `0x52` kit, `0x53` sound, `0x54` project settings; requests `0x60-0x64`, and `0x6F` asks for the whole project. So `0x54` is a Rytm pattern but a DT2/DN2 project-settings message. syxgrid's guess "`0x53` = kit" for the DN2 (graded D, unknown) is a sound dump by digi-roll's table. `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol} {syxgrid-map} — `sysex-and-midi#7642b2b0` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:35](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L35) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)

- [doc] Elektron Emu (xerydian): five VST3 plug-ins (Mac, Windows) running each machine's real OS in an emulated CPU - Digitakt II, Syntakt, Analog Rytm MKII, Digitone II, Model:Cycles; the user supplies the `.syx` in a per-machine folder; +Drive emulated and persisted, WAV loading on DT2/Rytm/DN2; Digitone II's DSP is compiled locally on first open (needs a C compiler; otherwise a slow interpreter that renders offline only); limits: Rytm analog voices are a custom model that does not sound like the machine, Syntakt analog tracks 9-12 missing; 2 commits, no licence stated. `[doc]` {elektron-emu} — `toolchain-and-emulators#d1f1bb43` [hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md:81](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md#L81) · Toolchains and emulators / More emulators and directory snapshots (2026-10-31)
- [doc] CPU: ColdFire MCF5445x (`-mcpu=54455`, big-endian) - like the Octatrack's family, not the MCF5441x of the small boxes. DDR from `0x40000000`, the OS at `0x40000400`, stack region `0x48000000`. `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#d4ecd72c` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:9](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L9) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Platform (MKII, OS 1.74)
- [doc] Sections of 1.74: 2 bootstrap (42,302 B, loads at `0x07020000`, runs in SRAM `0x80000000`), 1 FPGA (Xilinx bitstream, 149,516 B, sync `AA99`), 3 MAIN OS (3,005,432 B), 8 the shared ARM Cortex-M image (159,948 B, identical across several devices; see [firmware-container.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/firmware-container.md)), 5 meta. `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#2e2bae7f` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:10](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L10) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Platform (MKII, OS 1.74)
- [doc] The display is driven through the FPGA: a byte-FIFO bridge at `0xec07xxxx` (status `0xec070004`, data `0xec07000c`). The 128x64 panel uses two static 1,024-byte planes with diff flush. `0xec074xxx` is the MIDI UART (divisor 132 MHz / (31,250 x 32)). The LED engine is fed through the same FPGA SRAM family. `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#210d51fe` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:11](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L11) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Platform (MKII, OS 1.74)
- [doc] SPI NOR on DSPI `0xfc05c000`; layout: `0x00000-0x7FFFF` bootstrap + FPGA (never write), `0x80000+` the MAIN OS image. Images are staged in DDR at `0x3FF80008` with the same `size / checksum (i ^ word[i])` header as the small boxes. `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#8e9155bc` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:19](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L19) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Flash and recovery
- [doc] The bootstrap supports several flash vendors and picks the geometry from the RDID: | Vendor | Page | Erase block | |---|---|---| | Spansion `0x01 2018` | 0x200 | 0x40000 | | Winbond `0xEF` | 0x100 | 0x10000 | | Macronix `0xC2` | 0x100 | 0x10000 | | ISSI `0x9D` | 0x100 | 0x10000 | | EON `0x1C` | 0x100 | 0x10000 | The geometry therefore differs per unit. This very likely explains the two geometries reported for DT2/DN2 (CONFLICTS O8) and why a Spansion-only protection command does nothing on a Winbond unit (O9). `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#4db850ce` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:20](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L20) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Flash and recovery
- [doc] The bootstrap also gates on a version-date field (image +0x10, 4 ASCII chars) per chip family, and refuses older versions. `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#c91bdd6b` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:31](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L31) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Flash and recovery
- [doc] Board (static analysis, `[doc]`): same CPU family and OS framework as the MKII; ELE2 file with one section (MAIN OS); 128 MB DDR, boot/config flash as parallel NOR on FlexBus CS0 (8 MB at 0); voice SPI on DSPI2 with eDMA ch 29 (492-word frame, as the MKII); codec on SSI0 + SSI1 (8 words each); 122x32 LCD, 1-bit LEDs; USB full speed only. — `analog-rytm#a103cbd1` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:37](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L37) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Analog Rytm MK1 (OS 1.73 / 1.74)
- [doc] The bootstrap is inside MAIN OS, as on the A4 MK1 (rule A38): On 1.74 its version words are at `0x4028c768` and its image at `0x4028c770..0x402a1b84` (87,068 B, ending in its USB descriptors). On 1.73 the same image sat 0x60 lower. At every boot the startup code compares that version with the one in flash at `0x1fff8`. If the embedded one is newer, the OS shows BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE and rewrites the bootstrap sectors. `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#1cb9f433` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:45](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L45) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Analog Rytm MK1 (OS 1.73 / 1.74)
- [doc] Cached vs uncached DRAM: the chorus's delay line moved to a cached DRAM address (`0x428a0000`) in v2. The same rule applies as on the A4 MK1: don't touch uncached memory per sample. `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#fc52b0fb` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:56](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L56) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Analog Rytm MK1 (OS 1.73 / 1.74)
- [doc] Recovery: FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4 (OS UPGRADE), stock `.syx` over DIN MIDI (Transfer's legacy mode). `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#9a182ac2` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:62](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L62) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Analog Rytm MK1 (OS 1.73 / 1.74)
- [doc] Slots and claims: a mod machine takes one of the hidden slots 34-43 through `core_machines` and claims it as `machine:<slot>` (rule D6c). Kits store the slot, so a kit naming it loads as DISABLE on a build without the mod. `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#11c40054` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:66](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L66) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Mod machines in hidden slots (MKII OS 1.74, elekloader core-ar2 0.5; Modwerk's SDK guide, 2026-11-05)
- [doc] From core-ar2 0.13 (2026-11-10) also slots 44-52, the TEST machines. Their records carry no MIDI, so core copies each used knob's CC and NRPN from slot 35's record at the same sound index; the records' list-kind word (+0x24) stays 0, so a knob there is not offered as an LFO, velocity or aftertouch destination. Fewer knob records than 34-43 on several voices (e.g. SD TEST 9-12, 15, 16). `[doc]` {elekloader-core-ar2} — `analog-rytm#917eca81` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:67](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L67) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Mod machines in hidden slots (MKII OS 1.74, elekloader core-ar2 0.5; Modwerk's SDK guide, 2026-11-05)
- [doc] Per-voice trig and velocity (0.13): core's trampoline per slot latches the owner track (`0x40291138[v]`), the trig state (`0x8000e508 + 4t`, 1 trig, 2 release) and the velocity word (`0x800067c4 + 2t`) before the engine runs; `core_voice_trigged(v)` and `core_voice_velocity(v)` read it. A knob on a record that is 14-bit in stock keeps a fraction in its engine word: read the high byte for the shown value. `[doc]` {elekloader-core-ar2} — `analog-rytm#667c1103` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:68](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L68) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Mod machines in hidden slots (MKII OS 1.74, elekloader core-ar2 0.5; Modwerk's SDK guide, 2026-11-05)
- [doc] Knob ids: mods get their own parameter ids from 555 on; a mod declares `"knobs": n` and the linker hands out n ids in a row (`__knobs`). `[doc]` {elekloader-format} — `analog-rytm#15036b89` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:69](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L69) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Mod machines in hidden slots (MKII OS 1.74, elekloader core-ar2 0.5; Modwerk's SDK guide, 2026-11-05)
- [doc] Screen calls (0.13): text, fonts, bitmaps, the level read-out field, progress boxes and keys go through stock's own routines (font objects at `0x417e381c + 8i`, text `0x4007154c`, progress window as COPYING SOUNDS uses it); no stock code or glyphs are copied. `[doc]` {elekloader-core-ar2} — `analog-rytm#a6940d1d` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:70](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L70) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Mod machines in hidden slots (MKII OS 1.74, elekloader core-ar2 0.5; Modwerk's SDK guide, 2026-11-05)
- [doc] Fixed knob positions per slot (SYNTH page, sound indices): slot 40 A10 B13 C12 D11 / E14 F16 G15 H9; slot 41 A10 B13 C15 D11 / E16 F14 G12 H9; slot 42 A10 B12 C13 D11 / E16 F14 G15 H9. `knobs[k]` in `machines.h` is sound index 9 + k, not the panel order. Indices 9 (LEV), 10 (TUN) and 11 (DEC) keep stock's MIDI CCs. `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#1095d345` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:71](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L71) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Mod machines in hidden slots (MKII OS 1.74, elekloader core-ar2 0.5; Modwerk's SDK guide, 2026-11-05)
- [doc] Where it appears in the machine list: a 34-byte section table at `0x40257d70` (read by `0x400df664`) files stock machines 0-33 under a section; slots 34+ have no entry and sort above every stock machine of their group. A machine with `home` -1 lands after DISABLE in slot order. Core 0.5 adds a 4-byte entry (slot, section, 0, 0) so a mod machine sits under its section's header. The SY comparators (`0x400bdc5e`, `0x400bde1c`) rank only SY DUAL VCO, SY CHIP and SY RAW, so a mod SY machine sorts after them. `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#79170588` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:72](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L72) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Mod machines in hidden slots (MKII OS 1.74, elekloader core-ar2 0.5; Modwerk's SDK guide, 2026-11-05)
- [doc] FUNC + turn drops its first detent on the sound page (flag `0x417e32b8`); jumps come from a std::function in the parameter's RAM record (`0x419a4888 + 84 * id`, manager `+0x4c`, invoker `+0x50`). `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#bcb0071d` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:77](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L77) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Mod machines in hidden slots (MKII OS 1.74, elekloader core-ar2 0.5; Modwerk's SDK guide, 2026-11-05)
- [doc] Pick the narrowest assembler target that assembles. The project went from `-mcpu=5407` (ISA_A) to `-mcpu=5475` (ISA_B + EMAC) only when a mod needed EMAC, and checked that the earlier mods rebuilt byte-identically. Too narrow a target fails at assembly time; too wide a one silently accepts instructions the chip lacks (rule A42). `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#96a98856` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:81](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L81) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / More from the MKII mod and research projects (rytm-mods-src OS 1.73, analog-rytm-mkii-research OS 1.72)
- [doc] Sections 5, 2, 1 and 8 must come back byte-identical, and the bootstrap (section 2, 42,302 B at `0x07020000`) is checked by hash. Elektron's own bootstrap upgrade, which runs on the first restart after some OS updates, is the one moment the safety net is down: don't cut power then. `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#6d368869` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:82](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L82) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / More from the MKII mod and research projects (rytm-mods-src OS 1.73, analog-rytm-mkii-research OS 1.72)
- [doc] The master compressor is analog (after the analog mix and the master distortion). The MKII firmware never reads its gain back (the MK1 did, through the on-chip ADC input AN1), so any gain-reduction display on the MKII is an estimate. A CC beyond an enumeration's last value makes the unit show ERR instead of clamping. `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#c7614fe1` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:83](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L83) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / More from the MKII mod and research projects (rytm-mods-src OS 1.73, analog-rytm-mkii-research OS 1.72)
- [doc] Sample bit reduction is not done on the ColdFire. The BR knob becomes a per-voice command word, `0xB31407FF + ceil(BR x 0x40000 / 127)`, sent over DSPI1/eDMA to the external audio hardware. The main OS contains no mask or shift that would apply it to PCM. So sample playback processing on the Rytm MKII likely sits in the FPGA/voice hardware: a lead for research map T12. Static and emulator work only. `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#ada74524` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:84](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L84) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / More from the MKII mod and research projects (rytm-mods-src OS 1.73, analog-rytm-mkii-research OS 1.72)
- [doc] A third reading of the CPU: analog-rytm-mkii-research models the Rytm MKII as MCF5441x (conflict O14), with MAIN at `0x40000400` (2,903,032 B on 1.72) and the stack at `0x48000000`. `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#7e81f9da` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:90](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L90) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / More from the MKII mod and research projects (rytm-mods-src OS 1.73, analog-rytm-mkii-research OS 1.72)
- [doc] Porting MKII mods to the MK1: same code base, different data (gdeo607/rytm1_mods, OS 1.73) {rytm1-mods}: Most routines are byte-identical, but the parameter info record is 88 bytes on the MK1 and 84 on the MKII. UI glyphs and the screen differ (122 px wide on the MK1, 128x64 on the MKII), so anything that draws its own pixels needs a redesign, not new addresses. Every RAM address (`0x41xxxxxx`, `0x8000xxxx`) has to be found again. Each of these would have been a silent bug. `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#209b05a1` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:91](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L91) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / More from the MKII mod and research projects (rytm-mods-src OS 1.73, analog-rytm-mkii-research OS 1.72)
- [doc] Lock saves keep bits 14-1 of a lock word, so bit 0 is lost; test with odd values. `[doc]` {modwerk-rytm-machines} — `analog-rytm#3b552291` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:103](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L103) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Modwerk Rytm modules and stock behaviour (OS 1.74, 2026-11-10)
- [doc] A third Data route. The loader adds a `/mods` route to stock's Data router (the one Transfer and Elektroid use for `/projects` and `/soundbanks`), registered at `0x400a005e` in the resolver's getter; uploads travel in stock's data container (31-byte header, 12-byte footer with CRC-32; a stock 1.74 project reads family 2, device 5). Folders go three deep; stock's rename moves a folder only within its parent, so a move elsewhere is mkdir plus one move per item, as SAMPLES' MOVE does. `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#3e4bc6a9` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:117](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L117) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / +Drive mods loaded at boot (elekloader drive-loader-ar2 0.4, core-ar2 0.12, OS 1.74)
- [doc] Files on the +Drive need a 16-byte zero header. The files share the sample filesystem, and stock's SAMPLES browser lists every folder, `/mods` too. LOAD TO PROJECT reads a file's first 16 bytes as a sample header: a raw `.elemod` there hangs stock, and a project that holds one stalls the next OS upgrade at PREPARING until CREATE NEW (SB19). The loader writes 16 zero bytes in front of every file, which stock loads as an empty sample. `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#27050eb5` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:118](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L118) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / +Drive mods loaded at boot (elekloader drive-loader-ar2 0.4, core-ar2 0.12, OS 1.74)
- [doc] The link runs at boot from a site at `0x401009e0` in `main()`, after the +Drive is mounted and before audio and the UI task start; it skips when [NO] is held at power-on, when the eMMC or filesystem did not come up, or when a crash flag `/mods/.armed` from the last start is there (deleted about 10 s after the mods' inits ran). Its working memory (about 270 KB for the 4.3 MB area) comes from stock's heap and goes back after the link. The area runs from the flashed build's RAM end to `0x47FFF000`. `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#e813a50e` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:119](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L119) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / +Drive mods loaded at boot (elekloader drive-loader-ar2 0.4, core-ar2 0.12, OS 1.74)
- [doc] Stock's two-pane file view (the one SAMPLES and PROJECTS use, `0x400734f2`) hangs the UI when it is first shown with no row at all; stock's own lists never are empty (`..`, or 128 RAM slots). `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#a6d9f1cf` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:121](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L121) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / +Drive mods loaded at boot (elekloader drive-loader-ar2 0.4, core-ar2 0.12, OS 1.74)
- [doc] Stock fires one event per track per block, so two due in one block take that block and the next. Mutes and a track's held word apply when the trig fires, not when it is queued. Retrigs are not queued: they run on their own tick counter. A pattern change clears queued events from the change on. `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#dcf4600c` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:125](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L125) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Queued trigs: what a mod can see before a trig fires (Modwerk, OS 1.74, read from the code)
- [doc] "Loosened" bytes have a cost on stock: bytes that stock reads but always holds at one value (for example the 8 low bytes of the velocity and aftertouch route amounts, sound `+0x71/+0x74/+0x77/+0x7a` and `+0x8d/+0x90/+0x93/+0x96`) can carry mod data only if every stock reader is hooked. A project or dump using them is then not safe on unhooked firmware: a changed version long makes the record load at defaults, and a level LSB at 127 loads as 100. Bytes stock never reads are harmless there. See rule E3. `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#5f4b4d04` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:131](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L131) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Where a MKII mod can keep its own data (rytm-mods-src `re/subsystems`, OS 1.73, checked in 1.74 by byte match; static plus rytm-emu, nothing on a unit)
- [doc] Performance macros are engine state, not kit data: 12 words at `0x8000e57c + 2k` (0..`0x7f00`), glided each block (~22 ms) into `0x8000f774[0..11]`. Their setter `0x400b2bfe` raises no change notice, so the kit is not marked edited. CTRL IN 1/2 are ADC slots 0 and 1, smoothed and mapped each block by `adc_pedal_update` (`0x4013f1c8`). `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#e7e99172` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:132](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L132) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Where a MKII mod can keep its own data (rytm-mods-src `re/subsystems`, OS 1.73, checked in 1.74 by byte match; static plus rytm-emu, nothing on a unit)
- [doc] Track mutes belong to the project, scenes to the kit. Every UI and MIDI mute goes through `track_mute_set` (`0x400b786c`); Overbridge uses `track_mute_set_silent` (`0x400b6d6c`), which has no guard and bypasses hooks on the main setter. All scene engages (pads, CC 92, NRPN `0xE8`, Overbridge) go through `kit_scene_set_active` (`0x400a7d04`). `[doc]` — `analog-rytm#ea7bd3b0` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:133](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L133) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Where a MKII mod can keep its own data (rytm-mods-src `re/subsystems`, OS 1.73, checked in 1.74 by byte match; static plus rytm-emu, nothing on a unit)
- [?] Which ColdFire is open: rytm-fw-re builds with `-mcpu=54455` (MCF5445x), while analog-emu identifies the Rytm MKII as MCF5441x (same entry code, CACR/ACR values and peripheral blocks as the A4 MKII). Both are V4 cores with EMAC and no FPU, so code built for either runs; peripheral addresses are what to check. See CONFLICTS O14. `[?]` — `analog-rytm#7f44f829` [hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md:15](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md#L15) · Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Platform (MKII, OS 1.74)
- [untagged] What it is for is open (CONFLICTS O16). dnfw links it to the Outbox 8 accessory, because it arrived in the DN2 release that added Outbox support. analog-emu calls it the panel MCU firmware. Against that: the DN2, Rytm and A4 operating systems carry their own panel firmware inside MAIN and re-flash the panel from there. — `firmware-container#ec516aaf` [hardware/common/firmware-container.md:67](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/firmware-container.md#L67) · Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Section 8: one shared ARM firmware image (merged from dnfw, analog-emu, digikit, rytm-fw-re)
